rot.ideia.ex1.e1: Now the knight, which is on d4. He moves unlike any other piece.
rot.ideia.ex1.e2: His move has the shape of an L: two squares in a straight line and one more to the side.
rot.ideia.ex1.e3: From d4 his jumps reach eight squares.
rot.ideia.ex1.p: Take the knight to e6, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.certo: That's right! Two squares up and one to the right.
rot.ideia.ex1.revela: The knight jumps in an L to e6: two up, one to the side.
rot.ideia.ex1.fora: The knight jumped to another square of the L. Let's go back: the target is e6.
rot.ideia.ex1.volta: Take the knight to e6, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.l1: The L can turn any way: up, down, left or right.
rot.ideia.ex1.l2: For example, two squares left and one down, to b3.
rot.ideia.ex1.l3: Remember the idea: the knight moves in an L, always the same jump.
rot.ideia.ex1.l4: Now what only the knight does: jump over pieces.
rot.ideia.ex2.e1: Now the knight is on b1, with a row of white pawns in front of him.
rot.ideia.ex2.e2: No other piece could get past that row of pawns. The knight can: he jumps over.
rot.ideia.ex2.e3: He just cannot land on a square taken by a piece from his own side, like d2.
rot.ideia.ex2.e4: Your goal is to take the knight to e4, in two jumps.
rot.ideia.ex2.p: What is the first jump towards e4? Suggest one, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.certo: That's right! From c3 the knight already reaches e4.
rot.ideia.ex2.revela: The first jump goes to c3, over the pawn on c2.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.b1a3.1: From a3 the knight is still far from e4: no L gets there.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.b1a3.2: Let's go back and jump the other way.
rot.ideia.ex2.volta: What is the first jump towards e4? Suggest one, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.l1: From there, another L: two squares right and one up.
rot.ideia.ex2.l2: The pawns did not get in the way at all: the knight went over them.
rot.ideia.ex2.l3: Remember the idea: a piece in the way does not stop the knight; only the landing square matters.
rot.ideia.ex2.l4: You have now seen the knight's two rules. Now I will show them in other positions.
rot.demos.canto.e1: Look at the knight in the corner, on a1.
rot.demos.canto.e2: Here he has only two squares: b3 and c2.
rot.demos.canto.l1: Jumping to b3, he gets six squares again.
rot.demos.canto.l2: In the corner, the knight is weak. In the centre, he reaches much more.
rot.demos.trocaCor.e1: The knight is on e4, a light square.
rot.demos.trocaCor.e2: All the squares of his L are dark.
rot.demos.trocaCor.l3: With every jump, the knight changes the colour of his square.
rot.demos.casaVizinha.e1: The knight on e4 wants to go to e5, the square just above.
rot.demos.casaVizinha.e2: It looks close, but the L always takes the knight further than the next square.
rot.demos.casaVizinha.l3: ...and only on the third does he reach e5.
rot.demos.casaVizinha.l4: For the knight, the next square can be far away: count the jumps.
rot.demos.casaVizinha.l5: Now it's your turn: in the next positions, take the knight to the stars.
rot.pratica.estrelas1.enunciado: Take the knight to the three stars, stopping on each one, in any order you like.
rot.pratica.estrelas1.fim: Perfect. One L after another, the knight crosses the board.
rot.pratica.estrelas2.enunciado: Now there are pawns around the knight. Take him to the stars.
rot.pratica.estrelas2.fim: Well done. You now know how to move the knight: the L-shaped jump, over any piece.
